claim.pdf_says: The special-character-word table's column headings, printed once at the head of the table on page 135, are: "Word" and "Meaning". Page 136 is a continuation of that table and prints no heading row.
claim.markdown_says:
| Symbol | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| – | Arithmetic operator - unary minus or subtraction |
claim.why_it_matters: The continuation half of the table is given an invented heading row whose labels differ from the standard's own terms. 8.3.2.4.2 defines these entries as special character *words*; labelling the column "Symbol" instead of "Word" drifts from the spec's terminology, and "Description" replaces "Meaning". The page-135 half of the same table correctly uses `| **Word** | **Meaning** |`.

verdict.reasoning:
Both halves of the claim were independently checked against fresh 300dpi renders. PDF p136 (printed page 106): the page opens directly with the tabular entries — "–  Arithmetic operator - unary minus or subtraction", "*  Arithmetic operator - multiplication", ... through "::  Method invocation operator" — with NO heading row of any kind above them; the first printed heading on the page is the section heading 8.3.2.4.3 Optional words, below the table. PDF p135 (printed page 105) was rendered to check the claimed source labels: under "2) Special character words. The special character words are:" the standard prints a bold two-column heading reading exactly "Word" and "Meaning", and page-135.md transcribes that faithfully as `| **Word** | **Meaning** |`. So the claim misquotes neither source: "Symbol" and "Description" appear nowhere on p136 (or anywhere in this table), and the standard's own labels for these very columns are "Word" and "Meaning".

Refutation attempts, and why they only partly succeed: (1) The "missing text is actually present" test does not apply — this is inserted text, not lost text. (2) The page-break-furniture test partly applies: a GFM table cannot exist without a header row, so a table continued across a page boundary in a page-per-page transcription must synthesize SOME header. That structural necessity is legitimate furniture, and to that extent the claim overreaches by implying the header row itself is the defect. (3) The does-not-change-meaning test holds for the table body: all 15 entries (– * / ** & > < = == >= <= <> *> >> ::) are transcribed, in order, with correct meanings, and the wrapped continuation of the "=" entry ("and assignment operator in COMPUTE") is correctly joined onto its row. No normative content is lost or altered.

What survives: the defect is not the header row's existence but its label text. The synthesized scaffold fabricates two words — "Symbol" and "Description" — that are attributable to no line of the standard, and that contradict the standard's own naming of the same two columns one page earlier. In a transcription whose sole value is fidelity of terminology, inserting non-spec column names is a real (if minor) fidelity defect, distinct from expected furniture such as running headers, page numbers or `<a id="page-136">` anchors. "Symbol" is also substantively the wrong word here: 8.3.2.4.2 classes these as special character *words* (a category of reserved word), and 8.3.1.1's separate notion of a "symbol" makes the substitution actively misleading. Severity is correctly assessed as cosmetic — no rule, format or list content is affected.
verdict.corrected_description: CONFIRMED, with the scope narrowed. Page 136 of the PDF is a mid-table continuation and prints no heading row; the transcription's page-136.md opens the continuation with a synthesized header `| Symbol | Description |`. The existence of a header row is NOT the defect — a GFM table cannot omit one, so a page-per-page transcription must synthesize a header for any table split across a page boundary; that is legitimate page-break furniture. The defect is the label text: "Symbol" and "Description" are words that appear nowhere in the standard for this table, and they contradict the standard's own bold column headings for the same two columns, printed on page 135 and transcribed correctly there as `| **Word** | **Meaning** |`. "Symbol" is additionally the wrong term of art — 8.3.2.4.2 classes these entries as special character *words*, a kind of reserved word. Correct fix: change page-136.md's synthesized header to `| **Word** | **Meaning** |` so the continuation matches the standard's own labels. The table body is otherwise faithful — all 15 entries are present, in order, with the "=" entry's wrapped second line correctly joined. Severity cosmetic; no normative content is affected.
